Guidance & outlook: I also sincerely thank the board for their guidance and more so Keki Mistry for chairing as the Interim Chairman during this period.

I think while this quarter it could be a 20% mix in terms of deposits, etcetera, but I guess these things then normalize and in the medium to long term, I think it's been more or less stable, which is what we have seen over the last 10 years.
So any number if you can share or growth estimate outlook that we are targeting at.
Growth & demand: I mean on a quarter-to-quarter basis we can't see and we don't judge, but on a yearly basis for the year that went by, for example, March 26, for which data got published across the industry, while we grew between 9.5% - 10% or so, we still gained market share on that, right, on that front.
But 9.8% profit growth is still lower than the overall balance sheet growth correct.

Again, we've seen a growth of close to 14% in terms of disbursements on mortgages on year-on-year and the earlier two pieces that I talked about, we've seen disbursement growth approximately of about 20% odd.
Margins & costs: This quarter, you may see some amount of mix change in terms of more non-retail shorter-term asset mix, the cost of funds moderation, these are all elements which I believe are just tactically being managed.

There are two aspects as you know, one, the cost of funds is the biggest opportunity on the margin where compared to our historical norms as well as compared to what we have seen in the industry as such, there can be 40, 50 basis points change, but it is not going to change in a hurry.

So, this is about the unit economics that we need to drive and at the same time as we drive the unit economics, we are today little more than 100 million customers, and as we drive the unit economics, keep the cost in check and under control on efficiency so that we scale this.
Capex & expansion: I think these are the three or '25, ‘26, which is what we did and that was pretty much reflected in the slowdown in the new acquisitions because we were gearing ourselves to the new realm of better quality acquisitions.

I think as we move forward, I think we are reasonably confident that we not only should reach reasonable healthy numbers in terms of annual momentum depending on the capacity of the overall 9,700 branches, but also the quality acquisition value unit value as well.

So am I to understand that this, you know, decline in the CASA ratio is temporary or is a passing phase and as your, customer acquisition engine starts to fire in, we will see a restoration also seeing, you know, the share of wholesale deposits rise albeit not by a large amount, but it's gone up from 17% to 20%.
Balance sheet & cash: Obviously, all of us realize that security is going to be an extremely important part of our strategy and we are focusing on seeing how we can leverage on AI to augment our defence mechanisms as well.

So we do think that the maturity should take care of that to some extent and the overall growth should also take care of it to the balance of the extent because as the growth happens and you don't need to fund only through borrowing, so then the borrowing percentage will dwarf and come down.
If you just replace borrowings with time deposit or you envisage to replace with a mix of time and CASA, but only time little more than 100 basis points you will see.
Risks & challenges: As you know, we navigated during this period certain challenges over the last four months.
Of course, there are risks in the horizon in terms of the weather-related disruptions like El Nino and also the geopolitical situation in West Asia.
The second question, I mean one of the biggest aspects post the merger is that sharp decline in CASA down to 34%.

Growth & demand: We had estimated the system credit growth to be around 10.5% to 11.5%.
Deposit growth rate at 14.4% continues to grow faster than the credit growth, which is what we've always been doing.
Net income growth clocked at 11%, similar to the last financial year, whilst EPS growth of 10% versus 3% last year.
Margins & costs: Despite the drop in NIMs, the return on assets continue to be stable at 1.9% due to cost efficiencies with cost-to-income declining from 40.5% to 39.5% on a core basis and focus on quality growth reflecting in lower credit costs.
The pricing on the deposit, if you look at the transmission that has happened, it is only about 40 to 50 basis points that has come into that so far.
Srinivasan Vaidyanathan: The other one you talked about the cost of funds, I think we published the cost of funds, which is about 4.4% or so, marginally come down.
Capex & expansion: Customers at 100 million, we continue to acquire about 6 million to 8 million customers a year.

Guidance & outlook: At least if you see through large part of FY26, the nominal GDP growth expected was somewhere around the 9%, 9.5%, so one consensus until the large part of the year was a system credit growth of around 10.5% to 11.5%.
This is what we had expected, and we calibrated our strategies and our growth in line with that, and that is why we grew at 12%.
It is something that we have to navigate, but it's not too far away from the momentum we have seen from a 5.4% growth in FY25 to a 12% growth.
Risks & challenges: Now in terms of the volatile or the high frequency deposits, it's quite natural when you have corporate as a significant part of a corporate and capital markets, which contribute 55% or 53% of the balance sheet, you will have large relationships which you need to patronize.
And that aspect of the 15% of the total deposits will be volatile in nature.

More importantly, more than the 50% stock that we sit on, today approximately a little over 60% to 65% of that stock pays their EMI through my own account and which tells you the synergy which a home loan and a liability bring from a value accretion perspective as well as from a risk perspective.
Balance sheet & cash: The above is going to provide a huge operating leverage in the future.
The borrowings have come off almost 11% year-on-year, but the NIM trajectory is broadly similar with what some of your peers have reported.
But yes, changing of the borrowings mix is a favorable item where costs that are higher, essentially the spreads that you pay, you can save on that and get to the bottom.

India's GDP growth remained above the 7.0 per cent mark for the third consecutive year, with growth at 7.7 per cent in fiscal 2025-26.
